rapport_notes: Patient through repeated price/hours pushback from a customer worried about being overcharged for slow movers; never got defensive.

evidence_quotes.agenda: not asked — this is a follow-up call continuing a quote already submitted by email/text, not a fresh discovery call.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer: '...paying $300 an hour, I just don't see why they wouldn't just take their time.' Rep answered once with a professionalism/vetting reassurance, then moved on.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: if it ends six hours on the day of the move, then we will just charge you for six hours (beats-it-pay-less); our movers are professionally trained...not daily contracted workers (commit-to-rate/experience framing).

top_strength: Handled repeated pricing pushback patiently, adjusting crew size and hour commitment to fit the customer's own effort plan without breaking the minimum-booking logic.
coaching_note: Because this is a mid-negotiation follow-up, the opening discovery framing (quid pro quo, agenda ask) and Sheets 1/2 differentiators (damage coverage, Meet Your Mover) never got covered anywhere — build those into every touchpoint, not just the first call.
